slides.say: A machine makes sixty parts at a rate of thirty parts per hour, and then sixty more parts at a rate of twenty parts per hour. What is its average rate for all a hundred twenty parts, in parts per hour?
So the machine works at two different rates. They ask for one average rate for the whole job.
at: They ask for one average rate

slides.say: We'll solve it in three different ways. Let's start with the math way. A rate is the work over the time. So the average rate is the total work, over the total time.
at: So the average rate is the total work

slides.say: The total work is a hundred twenty parts. Now the time. Sixty parts at thirty an hour. The time is the work divided by the rate. Sixty divided by thirty is two hours.
Sixty more parts at twenty an hour. Sixty divided by twenty is three hours.
So the total time is two plus three, five hours.
A hundred twenty parts in five hours. A hundred twenty divided by five is twenty-four parts an hour.
at: A hundred twenty divided by five

slides.say: Careful with twenty-five, choice number one. That's the average of thirty and twenty. But the machine doesn't spend the same time at each rate.
So the average rate is twenty-four parts an hour. That's choice number two.

[pause] Now let's estimate. We start again from the givens. Sixty divided by twenty is three hours. Sixty divided by thirty is two hours. So the machine works three hours at twenty, and only two hours at thirty.
at: So the machine works three hours at twenty

slides.say: It spends more time at the slow rate. So the average is closer to twenty than to thirty. That means it's below twenty-five.
at: So the average is closer to twenty

slides.say: So twenty-five, choice number one, is out. And fifty, choice number three, is more than both rates, so it's out too.

slides: Twenty-two or twenty-four are left. The estimate can't decide between them, so let's use the seesaw.

slides.say: [pause] Remember the seesaw from averages. The hours are the weights here. So we put the two rates at the ends, twenty and thirty.
at: So we put the two rates

slides.say: Twenty has a weight of three hours, and thirty has a weight of two hours. So twenty is the heavy side.
at: Twenty has a weight of three

slides.say: Three plus two is five, so we cut the gap into five equal units. The gap is thirty minus twenty, ten. Ten divided by five is two. So each unit is two.
at: we cut the gap into five
The gap is thirty minus twenty

slides: The pivot is closer to the heavy side. It's two units from twenty, and three units from thirty.

slides.say: Two units is two times two, four. Twenty plus four is twenty-four. The same answer.

So whenever they ask for an average rate, we divide the total work by the total time. The plain average of the rates works only when the times are equal. Otherwise, the answer is closer to the rate with more time.
Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
